effect_claim: Across six sets of cartoons, higher aggressiveness ratings were positively associated with higher funniness ratings.
effect_claim_quote: The correlation of median humor and median aggressiveness rankings ranged from .49 to .90 in six studies
original_authors: C. McCauley, K. Woods, C. Coolidge, and W. Kulick
original_journal: Journal of Personality and Social Psychology
replication_title: Are Aggressive Cartoons Really Funnier? A Replication
replication_authors: Stefan Stieger and Anton K. Formann
replication_target_quote: parent study of McCauley and colleagues (1983)
outcome_quote: Aggressive or painful cartoons were not perceived to be funnier

effect_name: Sight over sound in music competition judgments
effect_claim: With brief clips of music competitions, observers identified winners from silent videos more reliably than from audio-only or audiovisual recordings.
effect_claim_quote: People reliably select the actual winners of live music competitions based on silent video recordings
original_title: Sight over sound in the judgment of music performance
original_journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
replication_title: Sight-over-sound judgments of music performances are replicable effects with limited interpretability
replication_authors: Samuel A. Mehr, Daniel A. Scannell, and Ellen Winner
outcome_quote: we successfully replicate this finding in a highly-powered sample but then demonstrate that the sight-over-sound effect holds only under limited conditions
review_note: The direct test using the original clips held, while follow-up tests found that the advantage depends on the specific recordings and task.

effect_claim: In a choice task, sadness increased the cash value participants gave up to obtain a good.
effect_claim_quote: Sadness also carried over, reducing selling prices but increasing choice prices
original_title: Heart Strings and Purse Strings: Carryover Effects of Emotions on Economic Decisions
original_authors: Jennifer S. Lerner, Deborah A. Small, and George Loewenstein
replication_title: The misery-is-not-miserly effect revisited: Replication despite opportunities for compensatory consumption
replication_authors: Nitika Garg, Lisa A. Williams, and Jennifer S. Lerner
outcome_quote: the effect replicated in the novel context

effect_name: False feedback changes cognitive control's contribution to IAT scores
effect_claim: False feedback that made racial prejudice salient increased the relationship between Stroop cognitive-control performance and race-IAT scores.
effect_claim_quote: increased the relationship with cognitive control (Stroop)
original_title: Manipulating the role of cognitive control while taking the implicit association test
original_authors: Eric F. Siegel, Michael R. Dougherty, and David E. Huber
replication_title: Cognitive Control and the Implicit Association Test: A Replication of Siegel, Dougherty, and Huber (2012)
replication_target_quote: We conducted two direct replications of Study 3
outcome_quote: weak to no support for the original hypotheses

effect_claim: Asking oneself 'Will I?' rather than declaring 'I will' increased goal-directed task performance and intentions.
effect_claim_quote: merely writing Will I as opposed to I will as part of an ostensibly unrelated handwriting task produced better anagram-solving performance
original_title: Motivating Goal-Directed Behavior Through Introspective Self-Talk: The Role of the Interrogative Form of Simple Future Tense
original_authors: Ibrahim Senay, Dolores Albarracín & Kenji Noguchi
replication_title: I Will Use Declarative Self-Talk . . . or Will I? Replication, Extension, and Meta-Analyses
replication_authors: Judy L. Van Raalte et al.
replication_target_quote: self-posed interrogative question ("Will I?") to declarative ("I will")
outcome_quote: found no significant group differences in motivation, perceived exertion, or performance

effect_name: Therapist progress feedback for predicted treatment failures
effect_claim: Giving therapists patient progress feedback improved psychotherapy outcomes for patients predicted to be at risk of treatment failure.
effect_claim_quote: improved outcome relative to patients in the control condition who were predicted to be treatment failures
original_title: The Effects of Providing Therapists With Feedback on Patient Progress During Psychotherapy: Are Outcomes Enhanced?
original_authors: Michael J. Lambert, Jason L. Whipple, David W. Smart, David A. Vermeersch, Stevan L. Nielsen & Eric J. Hawkins
replication_title: Enhancing psychotherapy outcomes via providing feedback on client progress: a replication
replication_target_quote: thereby replicating an earlier study using nearly identical methodology
outcome_quote: improved outcome for clients identified as potential treatment failures

effect_claim: Viewing pictures of natural settings improved directed attention measured with the Attention Network Test relative to urban settings.
effect_claim_quote: viewing pictures of nature can improve directed-attention abilities as measured with a backwards digit-span task and the Attention Network Task
original_title: The Cognitive Benefits of Interacting With Nature
original_authors: Marc G. Berman, John Jonides & Stephen Kaplan
replication_title: Conceptual replication study and meta-analysis suggest simulated nature does not reliably restore pure executive attention measured by the attention network task
replication_authors: Jennifer Adrienne Johnson, Brooke E. Hansen, Emily L. Funk, Francesca L. Elezovic & John-Christopher A. Finley
outcome_quote: simulated nature does not seem to reliably restore executive attention

effect_claim: An image of watching eyes led participants to judge moral violations more harshly than an image of flowers.
effect_claim_quote: Violations were more strongly condemned in a condition where participants were exposed to surveillance cues
original_authors: Pierrick Bourrat, Nicolas Baumard & Ryan McKay
replication_title: Effect of artificial surveillance cues on reported moral judgment: Experimental failures to replicate and two meta-analyses
replication_authors: Stefanie B. Northover, William C. Pedersen, Adam B. Cohen & Paul W. Andrews
replication_target_quote: effect of artificial surveillance cues on moral judgment
outcome_quote: we found no evidence that artificial surveillance cues impact reported moral judgment
review_note: Four direct experiments found no evidence for the original moral-condemnation effect; the paper's broader meta-analyses reported small or mixed evidence.

effect_name: Sight-word and phonics training improve word-reading fluency
effect_claim: Both sight-word and phonics training increased word-reading fluency in children with dyslexia.
effect_claim_quote: Both sight word training and phonics training had significant effects on word reading fluency
original_title: Sight Word and Phonics Training in Children With Dyslexia
original_authors: Genevieve McArthur, Anne Castles, Saskia Kohnen, Linda Larsen, Kristy Jones, Thushara Anandakumar & Erin Banales
replication_title: Replicability of sight word training and phonics training in poor readers: a randomised controlled trial
replication_authors: Genevieve McArthur, Saskia Kohnen, Kristy Jones, Philippa Eve, Erin Banales, Linda Larsen & Anne Castles
replication_target_quote: quasi-randomised trial of sight word and phonics training
outcome_quote: large and significant valid treatment effect on trained irregular words and word reading fluency
review_note: The word-reading fluency gain held for both training methods, while the sight-word group's reading-comprehension gain did not replicate.

effect_claim: Retrieval practice reduced later recall of previously studied targets compared with studying those targets twice.
effect_claim_quote: ultimately recalled fewer of those targets compared with a group of participants who studied the targets twice
original_title: The negative testing effect and multifactor account
original_authors: Daniel J. Peterson & Neil W. Mulligan
original_journal: Journal of Experimental Psychology: Learning, Memory, and Cognition
replication_title: Investigating the Replicability and Generalizability of the Negative Testing Effect
replication_authors: Kathryn T. Wissman & Daniel J. Peterson
replication_journal: Journal of Applied Research in Memory and Cognition
replication_target_quote: examining the original demonstration with a novel participant population
outcome_quote: Outcomes establish the replicability of the negative testing effect

effect_name: Imagined immoral contact evokes mental contamination
effect_claim: Imagining a forced kiss elicited more mental contamination than a consensual kiss; a consensual kiss from a moral man elicited the least.
effect_claim_quote: a non-consensual kiss evoked greater feelings of mental contamination than a consensual kiss
original_title: Analyses of mental contamination: Part I, experimental manipulations of morality
original_authors: Corinna M. Elliott & Adam S. Radomsky
replication_title: Mental contamination among people in China: A replication of a moral manipulation experiment
replication_authors: Tan Tang, Zhongfang Fu & Jianping Wang
replication_journal: Journal of Behavior Therapy and Experimental Psychiatry
outcome_quote: Unlike in that study, however, imagining a consensual kiss from a moral man also aroused strong mental contamination
review_note: The forced-versus-consensual contrast held, but the consensual kiss from a moral man produced substantial contamination, unlike the original pattern.

effect_claim: Rumination statistically mediated prospective associations between symptoms of depression and anxiety in adults.
effect_claim_quote: baseline depression predicted increases in anxiety and baseline anxiety predicted increases in depression; rumination fully mediated both of these associations
original_title: Rumination as a transdiagnostic factor in depression and anxiety
replication_title: Repetitive negative thinking as a transdiagnostic factor in depression and anxiety: A conceptual replication
replication_authors: Jolijn Drost, Willem van der Does, Albert M. van Hemert, Brenda W. J. H. Penninx & Philip Spinhoven
replication_target_quote: cross-sectional and prospective relations between anxiety and depressive symptoms
outcome_quote: changes in rumination mediated these associations
review_note: Conceptual replication: the original studied symptom co-occurrence, whereas this paper studied diagnosed disorders; rumination partly mediated the prospective link.

effect_name: Large multivariate sex difference in 16PF personality scores
effect_claim: Across 15 latent 16PF personality factors in a U.S. sample, the original study estimated a large male-female group difference (Mahalanobis D=2.71).
effect_claim_quote: the effect size for global sex differences in personality was D = 2.71
original_title: The Distance Between Mars and Venus: Measuring Global Sex Differences in Personality
original_authors: Marco Del Giudice, Tom Booth & Paul Irwing
replication_title: Global sex differences in personality: Replication with an open online dataset
replication_authors: Tim Kaiser, Marco Del Giudice & Tom Booth
outcome_quote: Our results corroborate the original study (with a comparable if somewhat smaller effect size)
review_note: The replication used an equivalent online 16PF-style questionnaire and found a large multivariate difference, but its D = 2.06 was smaller than the original D = 2.71.

effect_claim: Repeated statements are more likely than new statements to be judged as having been used as fake news on social media, regardless of their actual truth.
effect_claim_quote: repetition may also increase perceptions that statements are used as fake news on social media
original_title: Repetition increases both the perceived truth and fakeness of information: An ecological account
original_authors: Olivier Corneille, Adrien Mierop & Christian Unkelbach
replication_title: Robustness Tests Replicate Corneille et al.’s (2020) Fake News by Repetition Effect
replication_authors: Jérémy Béna, Olivier Corneille, Adrien Mierop & Christian Unkelbach
outcome_quote: repeated statements as having been previously used as fake news on social media more than new statements
review_note: Programming errors in the original led to a corrigendum; two preregistered replications with corrected programs reproduced the social-media fake-news judgment effect.

effect_name: Partner success lowers men's implicit self-esteem
effect_claim: Men show lower implicit self-esteem after thinking about a romantic partner's success than after thinking about a partner's failure.
effect_claim_quote: men's implicit self-esteem is lower when a partner succeeds than when a partner fails
original_title: Gender differences in implicit self-esteem following a romantic partner's success or failure
original_journal: Journal of Personality and Social Psychology
replication_title: Implicit self-esteem following a romantic partner's success: Three replications and a meta-analysis
replication_authors: Heather-Christina C. Hawkins, Tara L. Lesick & Ethan Zell
replication_target_quote: writing about a romantic partner's success versus failure
outcome_quote: the effect of writing about a romantic partner's success was not statistically significant
review_note: All three replication tests were nonsignificant; the pooled effect was small (d = 0.13), 78% below the original estimate. Two of the three were preregistered.

effect_claim: For previously unrecalled items, more practice tests before restudy improve subsequent learning compared with fewer practice tests when trial time is limited.
effect_claim_quote: unsuccessful retrieval attempts enhance the effectiveness of subsequent restudy
original_title: Test-potentiated learning: distinguishing between direct and indirect effects of tests
original_authors: Kathleen M. Arnold & Kathleen B. McDermott
original_journal: Journal of Experimental Psychology: Learning, Memory, and Cognition
replication_title: Test-potentiated learning: three independent replications, a disconfirmed hypothesis, and an unexpected boundary condition
replication_authors: Kathryn T. Wissman & Katherine A. Rawson
replication_target_quote: following more versus fewer practice tests
outcome_quote: more versus fewer tests potentiate learning when trial time is limited
review_note: Three independent replications supported the effect with brief trials; the effect weakened as trial length increased.
